text:
Recent work supports separating persistent taste, temporary intent, and recurrence. [DSLR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) extracts and evolves session-level interests for long-term modeling, while contrastive augmentation denoises short-term behavior. [HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=t0q7KbmB7o) is especially relevant: session hypergraphs and soft clustering identify latent intents; Hawkes processes model intent recurrence; multi-level attention captures recent interests. Recurrence operates at the intent level, potentially benefiting unseen-item recommendation even when previously consumed items are excluded.

Timing models offer a distinct signal from preference. [TSRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08531) combines repeat-behavior sequences with item-specific time intervals, although direct repeat-item scoring has limited applicability when recommendations exclude seen items. [MGUI (2026)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11506283) combines time-aware recent-item gates, group-level capsule/Transformer representations, global transition graphs, and user-specific expert fusion. These mechanisms capture several behavioral scales without requiring observed ownership. Learned transitions remain associations, however; they do not establish functional complementarity or replenishment needs.

Practical synthesis for SASRec: retain its recent-sequence encoder, add several pooled historical interest vectors, and learn candidate-dependent fusion with elapsed-time features and a directed item-transition score. Treat this as a proposed adaptation, not an established result. Ablate historical interests, recent intent, and timing separately using the common macro validation HR@10. Estimate temporal features solely from available history; avoid target timestamps unless supplied at inference. Infer latent groups from interactions or available text rather than unavailable product categories, ownership, or simulator traits. Published gains elsewhere do not establish improvement on this benchmark.
